About the opportunity Founded in 1998, HIAP – Helsinki International Artist Programme – is the largest international residency centre in the Nordic and Baltic region. Every year up to 40 artists and arts professionals residing in Finland and abroad are offered a working period at HIAP. With $15,000 in funding, this three-month residency program offers time and space for open-ended research and experimentation, without the requirement to produce finalised work. The HIAP residency venues are located on Suomenlinna island, a UNESCO World Heritage Site located a 15-minute ferry ride away from the centre of Helsinki, and in the Cable Factory cultural complex in Helsinki. The HIAP residency program focuses on visual arts, however, it is open to artists and curators from various disciplines. Collaborating with local and international partner organisations, residencies extend to such creative fields as dance, theatre, literature, and music. The activities are organised predominantly through thematic residency programs that highlight a geographical area or concentrate on a specific contemporary topic or an aspect of artistic practice. The HIAP residency program offers time and support for developing new work in dialogue with the local art scene. The goal is to offer space for experimental, cross-disciplinary art practices and to actively contribute to topical debates within and around the context of art. The HIAP team help the residents with their research as well as practical everyday matters. Residents have access to services such as weekly residency community meetings, facilities and equipment, and the option to take part in the HIAP Open Studios event. This normally takes place towards the end of each residency season and is an opportunity to present work-in-progress to arts professionals and the general public. More information can be found on the Helsinki International Artist Programme website . You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . The HIAP residency is a highly competitive opportunity. Past successful applicants typically demonstrated a clear rationale regarding the relevance of their proposal to the local arts scene and community. We encourage applicants to read through the assessment panel’s general feedback from the previous round and to contact us for advice. About this opportunity Through our partnership with Acme, visual arts professionals (including artists, curators, and arts writers) are offered a six-month residency at Acme’s East London Fire Station residency space. Founded in 1972, Acme Studios is a London-based charity that provides affordable studio space and residencies and awards for non-commercial fine artists. Acme supports over 800 individual artists across 8 boroughs in Greater London, offering a wide range of high-quality, long-term, and professionally managed artist studio spaces, including permanent new-build studios. In addition to affordable studio space, Acme operates a Residency & Awards programme which is one of the most supportive and extensive in the UK. Acme’s programme of artist support aims to intervene at pivotal moments in artists’ careers. Working with a range of international and UK-based partners and donors, the programme supports professional development for artists at all stages of their careers through residencies, bursaries, mentoring and exhibition opportunities. Over 800 artists have benefitted from the programme since its foundation in 1987. Acme makes every effort to assist visiting artists with the practical, cultural, and social aspects of their stay. In addition to managing the studio live/workspace, Acme works actively with visiting artists to assist with their networking, practical and research needs and allowing them to develop relationships and focus on their work in a supported environment. Acme staff are available to artists for residency pre-planning, local orientation and for assistance and advice throughout the residency. The overall aim of Acme’s Residencies & Awards Programme is to offer artists a supported environment and real professional development throughout the residency period. As every artist and their needs are different, Acme representatives are flexible about how they work with artists to achieve their goals. During the residency period, Acme provide resident artists with opportunities including: connecting with UK and international artists through Acme’s networks via Acme-organised events including gallery visits and social gatherings bespoke one-to-one studio critiques or mentor meetings with UK-based arts professionals, organised by Acme opportunity to work in collaboration with Acme staff to hold artist talks, or develop or participate in group discussions, critiques or events one-to-one ongoing support and discussion with Acme staff ongoing notifications and invitations to private views, open studios, lectures, and events in London. More information can be found on the Acme website . You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . About the residency The BR Whiting Studio residency is an opportunity for writers to direct their own program of activity and expand their practice and networks. There are three residencies on offer of varying duration: 1 x one month (with $6,500 support), 1 x three months (with $15,000 support), and 1 x six months (with $27,500 support). The Studio is an apartment in the Roman neighbourhood of Trastevere. It was given to Creative Australia by Lorri Whiting, an Australian abstract painter who was embraced by the Italian art scene. She spent many years living in Rome and exhibited in prestigious galleries across Italy, the UK and New York. She established the BR Whiting Studio as a gift to Creative Australia in honour of her late husband, the writer B.R ‘Bertie’ Whiting. The residency was originally established for the benefit of Australian poets and poets are encouraged to apply for the residency. Due to its location, the apartment can become hot in the summer months. Please take this into consideration when selecting your preferred residency period. Rome is a city rich in history, culture and religion. There are many opportunities for a writer to connect with bookshops, literary societies, universities, academics and translators. Residents are encouraged to make contacts prior to the commencement of their residency. Several previous residents have organised readings through universities and institutions such as the Keats Shelley House. About the opportunity Creative Australia is continuing the Debra Porch Award through its partnership with UNSW Galleries , Sydney and SAC Gallery , Bangkok. Artist Debra Porch’s practice focused on memory, mortality and the relationship between presence and absence. Working and teaching during art residencies in our neighbouring regions became vital in Debra’s art, work and life. In honour of Debra Porch’s life’s work, this reciprocal award seeks to continue to ensure long term engagement and strong intercultural connections across the Asia Pacific region. In 2027 the Award will be offered to two mid-careers artists - one from Australia and one from Thailand - who demonstrate a commitment to fostering long-term artistic and cultural connections between Australia and Thailand. One Australian visual artist will be supported to undertake a residency at SAC Gallery in Chiang Mai, Thailand. Alongside this, one mid-career Thai visual artist will also be supported to undertake a residency at UNSW Galleries in Sydney, Australia. Apply now About the opportunity The International Studio & Curatorial Program (ISCP) supports the creative development of artists and curators, and promotes exchange through residencies and public programs. Housed in a former factory in Brooklyn, with 35 light-filled work studios and two galleries, ISCP is New York’s most comprehensive international visual arts residency program. It was founded in 1994. ISCP organises exhibitions, events and offsite projects, which are free and open to all, sustaining a vibrant community of contemporary art practitioners and diverse audiences. Over 1,250 artists and curators from more than 75 countries, including the United States, have undertaken residencies at ISCP. The International Studio & Curatorial Program’s mission is: to support and enhance the professional development of emerging to mid-career artists and curators from around the world; to introduce New York audiences to exceptional international art practices; to engage communities of Brooklyn and the New York City area through public programs that enrich the appreciation and understanding of contemporary art. The International Program Residency opportunity at ISCP is for 4 months. While in the International Program, all residents are invited to participate in a number of activities in and outside of ISCP such as Visiting Critics, Field Trips, Salons and Open Studios. Please note that the ISCP will provide each resident a private and furnished studio space to work, however accommodation is not provided through this program. All residents at ISCP are encouraged to take advantage of the in-house community of artists and curators, offering invaluable international and local networks, professional conversations and critique. You can learn more about the studio, accommodation, local area, and travel arrangements by downloading the Information Pack PDF . More information can be found on the ISCP website . About the opportunity Matched Funding for Artists and Artist Groups – Intermediate supports artists to build on existing private sector fundraising experience and strengthen their practice over time. It is designed for artists and artist groups who have some private sector fundraising experience and are ready to develop more consistent and strategic approaches to private sector support. This opportunity provides matched funding alongside fundraising capability development through group training, peer-to peer learning and one on one support and advice. Matched funding is provided on a dollar-for-dollar basis for eligible private sector income raised, up to $10,000. The aims of the fund are for artists and artist groups to move beyond one-off or informal fundraising activity and develop consistent, strategic approaches to generating private sector support. Through participation, artists and artist groups will: build on existing private sector fundraising experience refine how they plan and deliver fundraising activity strengthen relationships with supporters increase confidence and independence as fundraisers. For the purposes of this application, an artist group is defined as two or more individuals who work together but do not form a legally constituted organisation. This can include co-collaborators and collectives. Matched Funding for Artists and Artist Groups – Intermediate is delivered through a structured fundraising capability development approach alongside matched funding. About the program Creative Australia’s Biennale Delegates Program is a professional development opportunity for individuals working in the visual arts sector (producers, technicians, writers, curators, artists, project managers) who are living in Australia. The program will facilitate an exchange of ideas, catalyse new perspectives, and support the seeding of future projects and collaborations. In 2026, the total intake for the program will be eight (8) individuals, one (1) representative from each State and Territory from across Australia. This program is for individuals: who are early career, within five to ten years of practice or experience as a creative practitioner interested in applying learnings from participation in the program to their practice wanting to develop or expand their national and global international networks wanting to explore shared global challenges to benefit Australian creative practice interested in identifying future international projects or collaborations from NSW, who live in Western Sydney. Create NSW defines Western Sydney as the thirteen local government areas of Blacktown City, Blue Mountains City, Camden Council, Campbelltown City, The City of Canterbury Bankstown, Cumberland Council, Fairfield City, Hawkesbury City, Liverpool City, The City of Parramatta, Penrith City, The Hills Shire, and Wollondilly Shire. The Biennale Delegates Program is a co-investment initiative with Create NSW, artsACT, Arts Tasmania, Arts Queensland, Create SA, Arts NT, and WA Government, and is philanthropically supported by the Cross Family Foundation. Program format In 2026, the Biennale Delegates Program returns as a distinctive initiative fostering creative exchange, critical dialogue, and professional development across global art platforms. Offering access to Australian and international events – including the Biennale of Sydney and Venice Biennale – the program positions delegates at the forefront of contemporary visual arts discourse. Developed and delivered by Creative Australia in a hybrid format, participants will shape their experience through curated workshops, mentorship with sector leaders, and collaborative learning. This immersive approach deepens understanding of curatorial practice, cultural mediation, audience engagement, and future-facing strategies shaping the arts. Delegates will need to commit to 14 days of in-person engagement in June and September, plus international travel. Support Successful applicants will receive a grant of AUD $4,750 to support their participation, professional development opportunities and outcomes. This grant includes: $400 allowance for the Sydney intensive to cover additional meals, airport transfer and incidentals. $850 allowance for the Venice, Italy intensive to cover additional meals, airport transfer and incidentals. This six-week onsite residency invites artists working across disciplines to explore the intersections of mental health, distress, and the ways pain—physical, psychological, and historical—shapes both individuals and societies. Applicants are encouraged to examine how suffering is distributed across race, caste, class, gender, and geography, and how people and communities navigate, resist, and reclaim vitality in the face of war, colonial legacies, and systemic inequality. The program offers a supportive and welcoming environment where artists can connect, share current work, and participate in constructive peer critique sessions. Across four weekly online sessions, participants will take part in ‘show and tell’ style discussions focused on artwork feedback, creative development, and building confidence within a community of peers. Sessions are intentionally small, with up to eight artists per group. The program will be facilitated by Dr Holly Arden (Flying Arts; former Director of Townsville City Galleries) and Alison McDonald, a Gurambilbarra/Townsville-based artist and recipient of the 2025 Art for Life Award at the Queensland Regional Art Awards. Participants can choose between a morning or afternoon session running across the following Mondays: July 6 July 13 July 20 July 27, 2026 Morning sessions run from 10:00am – 11:15am, while afternoon sessions run from 3:30pm – 4:45pm. The program is suitable for artists aged 18+ working across all media who are open to giving and receiving thoughtful and constructive feedback. Applications close Friday June 5, 2026 at 4:00pm. Nancy Fairfax Artist in Residence Studio – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Nancy Fairfax Artist in Residence Studio Deadline: Deadline: May 4 The Nancy Fairfax Artist in Residence Studio is a live-in, on-site residency program designed for visual artists living and working in Australia. Set within the grounds of Tweed Regional Gallery, the residency supports creative development while fostering meaningful engagement between artist, community, and place. The program offers a unique opportunity to work in a purpose-built studio with views to Mt Warning / Wollumbin, encouraging reflection, experimentation, and connection to the surrounding landscape. Self-Funded Residency: Artists can apply to undertake a subsidised residency, with studio rental fees of up to $400 per week (+ GST). This pathway is ideal for artists seeking dedicated time and space to develop their practice independently, with no requirement for an outcome exhibition or public programming. Funded Residency: Funded residencies are offered through invitation or specific partnerships. One annual residency is awarded to a Master of Fine Art (Painting) graduate from the National Art School, culminating in an exhibition in the Friends Gallery. Additional invited residencies are supported through philanthropic and institutional partnerships. This residency is well-suited for artists looking to immerse themselves in a focused creative environment while being supported by a respected regional gallery context. https://gallery.tweed.nsw.gov.au/discover/artist-in-residence-studio 0266702790 tweedart@tweed.nsw.gov.au

The prize is open to entrants from all across Australia over the age of 16. Mosman council funds the prize and acquires each year’s winning artwork, forming the basis of the Mosman Art Collection. Now in its 79th year the Mosman Art Prize has provided a historical timeline of contemporary painting practice in Australia. Mosman Art Prize Established in 1947, the Mosman Art Prize is Australia’s oldest local government art award. Artists from all Australian states and territories are selected as finalists for the exhibition in a professional public gallery space, with the overall winner rewarded a $40,000 cash prize donated by long time sponsors BSPN Architecture. Mosman Art Prize is Australia’s premier open painting prize. Established in 1947, the Prize has become a defining platform for contemporary Australian painting; a place where ideas, identity, and the spirit of our times are expressed through the enduring power of paint. As a national acquisitive prize of $70,000, funded by Mosman Council, the Mosman Art Prize celebrates painting’s unique ability to tell stories, capture moments of change, and reflect the complexities of contemporary life. It continues to foster conversations about who we are and how we see the world, making it a vital cultural touchstone for both artists and audiences alike. The Mosman Art Prize supports and elevates artists whose work engages with the present moment, while also contributing to the broader history of Australian art. The winning works form the heart of the Mosman Art Collection, a significant and vital public collection that traces the trajectory of Australian painting through decades of artistic innovation and expression. This year’s winning painting will go into the Collection and sit alongside such esteemed artists as Cressida Campbell, Grace Cossington Smith, Lucy Culliton, Guan Wei, Adam Cullen, Nicholas Harding, Lloyd Rees, Guy Warren, Margo Lewers, Jumaadi, Elisabeth Cummings, Natasha Walsh, Michael Zavros and Margaret Olley – who was the inaugural winner in 1947 Entries Close Monday 13 July, 11.59pm there will be no admin assistance past 5pm. How many entries can I submit? Entrants can submit up to two entries. I have an artwork that is created using only oil pastel. Can I enter it? No, the Mosman Art Prize is for paintings created using wet painting media, oils, acrylics or watercolours. Your artwork can be mixed media however the work must be substantially painted in order to qualify. Can I use AI (Artificial Intelligence)? No, the Mosman Art Prize only accepts original artworks from the artist. What size artworks do you accept? 2 metres² (2 metres squared) is the largest size an artwork can be, this includes framing. Artworks may be single or multi-piece as long as they do not exceed the overall dimensions, this includes the specified spaces between pieces of an artwork. Applications Call for Applications Open :: 2026 ANAT Synapse residency program ANAT is now calling for applications to the 2026 ANAT Synapse residency program and welcomes submissions from Australian artists who work in any genre with conceptual aims that intersect and deeply engage with science and/or technology. ABOUT The program brings artists and researchers together in partnerships that generate new knowledge, ideas and processes beneficial beyond both fields. A distinguishing feature of the residencies is their creative research focus , with applicants supported in collaborative experimentation rather than anticipating or producing specific outcomes . To ensure suitability between the artist and host organisation, a joint application must be submitted, led by the artist . It is the responsibility of the artist to identify the nature of the proposed research collaboration and establish a dialogue with their intended host prior to application. The successful artist will undertake the residency in 2026 across 16 weeks full time (or the part-time equivalent). We invite you to apply to become part of this expanding community of cross-disciplinary collaborators in the 2026 round. HOW TO APPLY The program is highly competitive. We encourage you to read the application guidelines carefully for further information and eligibility details. We also recommend you read the FAQs before applying. If you have any questions that aren’t covered, or would like further clarification about applying, please contact us at the details below. To apply, complete the online application form by 3 pm (ACDT), Wed 29 October 2025. APPLY HERE A one-page budget template can be downloaded here (choose ‘file’ > ‘download’). Please reach out to us if you encounter any issues when using the form. Our contact details are listed below. KEY DATES: Deadline for applications: 3 pm (ACDT), Wednesday 29 October 2025 Notification of outcome: December 2025 Residency period: Between February and October 2026 CONTACT Telephone: 08 8231 9037 Email: [email protected] FURTHER INFORMATION You can view the work of previous ANAT Synapse residency program recipients here: 2025 | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 | 2021 | 2020 | 2019 | 2018 | 2017 | 2016 | OLDER ANAT is assisted by the Australian Government through Creative Australia and the South Australian Government through CreateSA. ANAT and our project partners acknowledge and pay respects to the First Nations of the land known as Australia. We recognise all Traditional Owners and their continued cultural, spiritual and technological practices. We also acknowledge and pay respects to all First Nations peoples beyond Australian shores. As the very first storytellers, First Nations peoples hold invaluable knowledge and perspectives that are vital in the research, interrogation and development of traditional and emerging technologies, across both our physical and digital realms. Together we are gathering across many unceded lands that have been forcibly colonised. ANAT works on Kaurna yarta.

061af7906af4e03b742c8f99fe5865dc5e806e73.title: 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open
061af7906af4e03b742c8f99fe5865dc5e806e73.summary: 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open 2026 UMSU Art Prize: Entries Now Open The UMSU Art Prize returns in 2026 to celebrate the legacy of artistic talent and creative labour in Australian student unionism. Entries close Sunday 16 August, midnight. ex-upcoming no-news UMSU and the George Paton Gallery invite submissions from currently enrolled University of Melbourne students working across all visual art and design mediums. The UMSU Art Prize is a biennial award presented by the University of Melbourne Student Union, celebrating the creative practices of currently enrolled University of Melbourne students. Presented at the historic George Paton Gallery, the Prize provides a platform for innovative, critical and experimental artistic practices across visual art and design. Student voices give shape and clarity to the troubles of the present, hope for the future, and lessons of the past — this is your opportunity to add your voice to chorus. ENTRIES CLOSE SUNDAY 16 AUGUST 2026, MIDNIGHT AEST. APPLY NOW VIA OUR ONLINE FORM The UMSU Art Prize offers two awards: $5,000 UMSU Art Prize $1,000 People’s Choice Award Shortlisted artists will have their artworks displayed in the George Paton Gallery for the UMSU Art Prize 2026 exhibition, presented from 17 September to 9 October 2026. The 2026 Judging Panel is comprised of Hannah Presley (Senior Curator, Museums and Collections at University of Melbourne); Brigid Moriarty (Curator, Gertrude); and Sabrina Alday (Arts and Diplomacy Programs Lead, Asialink) The UMSU Art Prize will be announced at the opening event on Friday 18 September, and the People’s Choice Award will be announced on the final day of the exhibition, Friday 9 October. Please note, the Award is non-acquisitive. UMSU ART PRIZE SELECTION CRITERIA The following criteria will be used to assess submissions by the shortlisting panel and guest judges: Artistic Merit: The originality, creativity and technical skill demonstrated in conveying conceptual ideas. Engagement: The effectiveness of the artwork in connecting with a broad audience. Student Powered: The perspective of a student is one that is informed, curious, and analytical. It is important to see these qualities emerge from submitted work, to demonstrate the strength of the student voice. UMSU ART PRIZE SHORTLISTING All submitted artworks will be reviewed by the UMSU Arts and Culture Selection Panel between 3 and 14 August 2026. KYOTO ART CENTER Pictured Shinya Takeda of Kojima Shouten and Jenna Lee in the Kojima Shouten workshop in Kyoto About the opportunity The Australia Council for the Arts – in partnership with Kyoto Art Center – is offering an Australian visual artist the chance to live and work in Kyoto, Japan, as part of a residency exchange program. In 2020, one Australian visual artist will experience a two-month studio residency at Kyoto Art Center, a multi-art form venue in Kyoto. Kyoto Art Center houses a number of performance halls, exhibition spaces and artists’ studios, and acts as a hub for visual arts and dance organisations in Kyoto and across Asia. Residents at Kyoto Art Center work alongside other international and Japanese artists and can engage in local cultural activities, such as tea ceremonies, traditional performances and workshops. This residency is suitable for visual artists with interdisciplinary practices. The selected Australian artist will have access to a studio inside Kyoto Art Center, and separate accommodation at a private apartment, located 10 minutes walk from the Center. The Australia Council will award the selected artist a $7,500 grant as living and travel allowance. In the reciprocal arrangement, Kyoto Art Center’s selected Japanese artists: Nanao Tsukuda completed a residency at Artspace, Sydney from 22 July to 20 September 2018; and Kenichi Ishiguro, selected in 2021, will live and work at Parramatta Artists’ Studios in April and May 2024. Current resident: Jenna Lee Expand all Collapse all Eligibility Please check the general eligibility requirements on the Australia Council website. Selection Criteria Applications will be assessed by the Australia Council, in consultation with Kyoto Art Center and industry advisors, against the following selection criteria. 1. Potential of the artist/artists: quality of work previously produced artistic merit ability, skills and creative thinking that suggests strong artistic potential public or peer response to work previously produced. 2. Viability: the skills and artistic ability of the people involved and their relevance to the proposed activity realistic and achievable planning, resource use and evaluation the role of any partners involved, including confirmation of their involvement proposals which involve working with diverse audiences or communities, peers will look for demonstrated cultural competencies and appropriateness. 3. Impact on career: how the proposed activity strengthens your artistic practice the relevance and timeliness of the proposed activity how the proposed activity enables you to discover and develop new markets, or meet existing market demand how the proposed activity strengthens your capacity as an arts professional. Diversity and access The Australia Council encourages applications from applicants who identify as First Nations, from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with disability, and people living in regional and remote areas. fa004bd454e71704ad5b2c3f80aab4a5598ba329.summary: Amplify Creative Fellowships | Creative Australia Skip to main content Please note : to apply you must be registered in our application management system a minimum of two business days prior to the closing date Circus Community arts and cultural development Dance Disability Arts Emerging and experimental arts First Nations Arts Literature Multi-art form Music Theatre Visual Arts Closed Amplify Creative Fellowships Creative Australia, through the Australian Cultural Fund (ACF), has partnered with the Sidney Myer Fund (SMF) to support outstanding early mid-career Australian creatives and cultural leaders through the Creative Fellows program. The Australian Cultural Fund is operated by Creative Australia and has endorsement as a deductible gift recipient confirmed by the Australian Tax Office. Amplify Creative Fellowships Key dates Applications open: Wednesday 1 July Applications close: Sunday 9 August, 12am (AEST) Amount: $200,000 More information Sidney Myer Fund Website Contemporary Asian Australian Performance (CAAP), Longhouse. Photo: Jay Patel The Amplify Creative Fellowships provide unrestricted, tax-free grants of $200,000 over two years to individual Australian artists, creatives, and cultural leaders. Specific outcomes for the Fellowships are not required. Nomination and selection process Nominations are welcome for individual artists, creators, and cultural leaders throughout the spectrum of the arts, from visual and performing to interdisciplinary, new media, literature, and the humanities. All nominations must be submitted through the Sidney Myer Fund's SmartyGrants portal . Nominations that are recommended by an industry advisory panel form the basis of a shortlist, from which the Sidney Myer Fund’s Arts & Culture Committee then recommends recipients. These recipients will register via the Australian Cultural Fund to receive their fellowship payments To apply for an Amplify Creative Fellowship, applicants must be nominated by a third-party individual. Nominations are welcome for artists, creators and cultural leaders across the entire spectrum of the arts and humanities. In the online nomination form, applicants must also include: No more than five items of support material. This includes audio and/or visual files, support letters, and an artist CV of no more than two pages. Two referees who are not the nominator. To be eligible for Amplify Creative Fellowships, an applicant must: Be a minimum of 18 years old. Be an Australian citizen or Permanent Resident of Australia. Be at least seven years into their creative practice. Primarily reside in Australia for the two years of their Fellowship. Nominations are reviewed by a national panel of industry advisors with consideration to two criteria: Outstanding talent Exceptional courage Specifically, this talent and courage relate to the nominee's creative practice (commonly illustrated through artistic challenges, daring innovation, breaking new ground, and redefining the possible) and not to surmounting hardships. For more information on the nomination process and selection criteria, visit the Sidney Myer Fund website. Amplify Amplify is a program of the Australian Cultural Fund that provides administrative and operational capacity building support to Australia’s PAF sector to assist in distributing funds to the arts and cultural sector. Amplify allows PAFs to provide support for individual artists and organisations, allowing PAFs to direct funds where they are needed most within the arts and cultural sector. Amplify provides a system to ease the administrative grant-making load on PAFs engaged in arts funding, allowing PAFs to utilise best-practice processes without needing to develop them from the ground-up. australianculturalfund.org.au/amplify/ The Australian Cultural Fund is operated by Creative Australia, ABN 38 392 626 187, and has endorsement as a deductible gift recipient (DGR) confirmed by the Australian Tax Office. Presented by the Castlemaine Art Museum, the Len Fox Painting Award is a biennial acquisitive painting prize and is awarded to a living Australian artist to commemorate the life and work of Emanuel Phillips Fox (1865–1915), the uncle of Len Fox, partner of benefactor Mona Fox. The Len Fox Painting Award and generous acquisitive cash prize of $50,000 is funded through a bequest from Mona Fox. The Len Fox Painting Award recognises and promotes the work of Australian artists pursuing the artistic interests and qualities of E. P. Fox. These include engagement with colour and light; ambitious connections with international developments in art; and an interest in travel and an engagement with the cultures of diverse regions and peoples. The Len Fox Painting Award will be made to a painting judged to have addressed the interests of E. P. Fox as an imaginative, inquisitive, and worldly artist. Any style or genre is eligible; however, it is recognised that E. P. Fox is most noted for landscape, figurative and portrait paintings. The painting may be made in any medium, subject to declared practical limitations. This is an acquisitive award, with the winning work becoming part of the Museum’s Art Collection. Your organisation must demonstrate a high degree of artistic achievement, along with a compelling four year vision for the 2029–32 period. 20b7a2aac36e6fb6e787607877749eef34044799.summary: Neon Marketplace | Championing NSW Music Database Opportunity Championing NSW Music Database A new database to help NSW Government agencies find your music for future opportunities. Opportunity closes 30 Jun 2027 Connect with Sound NSW Sound NSW Enquiries Get in touch Connect with Sound NSW Sound NSW Enquiries Get in touch Connect with Sound NSW Sound NSW Enquiries Get in touch ROSHANI performing at Bluesfest, Byron Bay Photo by Lachlan Douglas Details NSW is home to extraordinary music that celebrates our stories, our people and our sense of place. In recognition of this important contribution, the NSW Government has introduced the Championing NSW Music Policy , which encourages government agencies to prioritise NSW music in their campaigns, initiatives and events. To help government agencies build their knowledge of the talent our state has to offer, Sound NSW is conducting a call out for NSW artists/acts and songwriters to join a database of NSW music professionals, called the Championing NSW Music database. The database will act as a resource to help government agencies discover NSW talent for consideration for use. This might include live performances at events, bespoke commissions for advertising campaigns, synchronisation opportunities for video/social media content, or the inclusion of music in playlists for events. If you are a NSW artist/act or songwriter (or represent one), and you would like to be included in the Championing NSW Music database, please fill out the form below . How to get involved Complete the submission form here . Please note that submitting your details to this database does not guarantee future work from the NSW Government. However, it will increase the opportunity to be contacted for NSW Government projects, initiatives and events. For more information on the Championing NSW Music database including how your information will be used, please visit the Frequently Asked Questions . Open Call for “Our Photo Books”

The ”Our Photo Books“ touring exhibition (Shanghai), coorganised by Yu Shaoyan Art Studio shaoyan_yu and 南荻纵生 NOMAD NO MAD SPACE, is now accepting submissions for its exhibits.

Submission Email: 340418598@qq.com
Please indicate the subject: Our Photo Books (Shanghai) + Your Name. 

Also include your contact information in the email.
Submission deadline: September 6, 2026

Requirements:
01. Submissions must be either a physical, original photograph or a photography book that is designed, institutional, or collectible. No restrictions apply to theme, style, materials, or age.

02. We particularly encourage submissions of self-published photography books handmade by the photographer.

03. Each photographer may submit only one photography book for the exhibition. Books will be displayed but not sold.

04. Please send your submission to the email address above. Include images of the book’s interior pages, flip-through videos, portfolio PDFs, video links, book descriptions, personal bios, or similar materials. Submit these as separate files or combine them into a single PDF for review.

05. Participation and exhibition are free of charge. Photographers are responsible only for postage.

06. Copyright remains with the original author. Books are loaned solely for the touring exhibition and will be returned after the event or may be used for the next stop on the tour.

bef57430d011a311bc9bf597c4575b59a7ab7f61.title: We’re happy to announce a new partnership and a new prize for the 5th year of Prisma Art Prize: a re
bef57430d011a311bc9bf597c4575b59a7ab7f61.summary:
Source: Instagram #artprize
We’re happy to announce a new partnership and a new prize for the 5th year of Prisma Art Prize: a residency award with The Nomadic Art Institute (Sardinia).

The Nomadic Art Institute is a non-profit organisation dedicated to contemporary art research and experimentation. Based in Sardinia and active between Laerru and Martis (Anglona), it treats the territory as an active field of inquiry—where landscape, history, and memory become starting points for shared research. Its work also includes the cultural programme of the Pinacoteca Contemporanea and the festival Ethno’s Arti Visive.

Residency prize (Martis, May 2027) includes: private accommodation + dedicated studio, airport transfers (and local support if needed), access to a fully equipped kitchen (meals self-managed), professional networking, and optional cultural/educational activities.

A sincere thank you to Eleonora Angiolini and Davide Tuseddu for making this collaboration possible.

Submissions for the 20th edition are now open — apply via the link in bio.

4b055f357f6a7002398f73e88985bed162467496.title: *OPEN CALL* Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen
4b055f357f6a7002398f73e88985bed162467496.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
*OPEN CALL* Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen 

Koloniale patronen zijn overal om ons heen; zichtbaar in de kleding die we dragen, de materialen en stoffen die we gebruiken en de handelsroutes die onze wereld hebben gevormd. In motieven, tradities en productieprocessen, maar ook in machtsverhoudingen, herinneringen en identiteiten. 

Voor de Textiel Biënnale 2027 nodigen we (inter)nationale kunstenaars uit om vanuit hun eigen praktijk en perspectief te reflecteren op het thema Koloniale patronen. Je kunt tot 1 oktober 2026, 12.00 uur een voorstel indienen via museumrijswijk.nl. 

De Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen vindt plaats van 8 juli tot en met 21 november 2027. 

*OPEN CALL* Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns

Colonial patterns are all around us; visible in the clothing we wear, the materials and fabrics we use, and the trade routes that have shaped our world. In motifs, traditions, and production processes, but also in power relations, memories, and identities.

For the Textile Biennial 2027, we invite (inter)national artists to reflect on the theme of Colonial patterns from the perspective of their own practice and perspective. You can submit a proposal via museumrijswijk.nl until October 1st, 2026, at 12:00 PM.

The Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns takes place from July 8 to November 21, 2027.

SUBMISSIONS ARE NOW OPEN | WORKS ON PAPER 2027

Green & Stone is delighted to announce the sixth edition of Works on Paper, our annual international open call and exhibition celebrating work made on, or with, paper.
Works on Paper 2027 will be particularly special. Opening in January, it will be the first exhibition of Green & Stone’s centenary year, beginning our celebration of 100 years since Green & Stone was founded in Chelsea in 1927.

We are inviting artists to submit work across drawing, watercolour, printmaking, collage, illustration, book arts, mixed media and experimental approaches to paper. We welcome submissions from artists at every stage of their practice, from emerging artists to established names.

Selected works will be exhibited at The Gallery at Green & Stone in London from 11 January – 3 February 2027, alongside a programme of events celebrating paper, materials and making.

Key dates
Submissions close: 12 noon, Wednesday 25 November 2026 Results announced: Wednesday 2 December 2026 Exhibition: 11 January – 3 February 2027 Private View: Tuesday 12 January 2027

Full submission details, eligibility, entry fees and terms can be found via the link in our bio.

Join us for this very special anniversary exhibition. We cannot wait to see what you have been making.

Artwork hollyfrean

Source: Instagram #artgrant
Ein großer Name als Referenz hilft nichts, wenn er deine Arbeit nicht kennt. Jurys merken das.
Was bei Referenzen zählt:
Wähl Menschen, die deine Praxis wirklich einschätzen können - Kurator:in, Lehrende, Kolleg:in mit Einblick.
Frag mindestens 3-4 Wochen vor Frist an, nicht zwei Tage vorher.
Gib der referenzgebenden Person Kontext: Ausschreibung, Frist, worauf sie eingehen soll.
Ein Empfehlungsschreiben ohne konkreten Bezug zur Arbeit wirkt generisch und fällt auf.
Lieber eine ehrliche, spezifische Referenz als zwei prominente ohne echten Bezug.
Speichern für die nächste Bewerbung.

Save. Beim nächsten Antrag dankst du dir selbst.

Schick's der Person aus deiner Klasse, die das gerade braucht.

🎨 OPEN CALL — HARMONY 🎨

Indra Gallery | 31st October

What does harmony mean to you?

Harmony can be found in many forms — in the balance between light and shadow, colour and form, movement and stillness. It can exist between people, cultures, nature, or within ourselves.

For this exhibition, we invite artists to explore the many faces of Harmony:

🌿 Harmony with Nature — our relationship with the natural world, cycles, landscapes, and living things.

🤝 Harmony Between People — connection, community, empathy, collaboration, and the beauty of coexistence.

🌓 Inner Harmony — balance within ourselves, between thought and emotion, chaos and calm, solitude and connection.

🎨 Harmony in Art — colour, composition, texture, rhythm, contrast, and the visual relationships that bring an artwork together.

⚡ Harmony in Contrast — the idea that opposing elements can coexist: light and dark, softness and strength, order and chaos.

🌍 Cultural Harmony — different traditions, identities, histories, and perspectives coming together without losing their individuality.

🎶 Harmony & Rhythm — repetition, movement, sound, pattern, and the invisible rhythms that shape our lives.

✨ Harmony in the Everyday — finding beauty and balance in ordinary moments, spaces, relationships, and experiences.

We welcome artists working across painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, mixed media, textiles, digital art, and other visual practices to interpret the theme in their own way.

museumrijswijk *OPEN CALL* Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen 

Koloniale patronen zijn overal om ons heen; zichtbaar in de kleding die we dragen, de materialen en stoffen die we gebruiken en de handelsroutes die onze wereld hebben gevormd. In motieven, tradities en productieprocessen, maar ook in machtsverhoudingen, herinneringen en identiteiten. 

Voor de Textiel Biënnale 2027 nodigen we (inter)nationale kunstenaars uit om vanuit hun eigen praktijk en perspectief te reflecteren op het thema Koloniale patronen. Je kunt tot 1 oktober 2026, 12.00 uur een voorstel indienen via museumrijswijk.nl. 

De Textiel Biënnale 2027 | Koloniale patronen vindt plaats van 8 juli tot en met 21 november 2027. 

*OPEN CALL* Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns

Colonial patterns are all around us; visible in the clothing we wear, the materials and fabrics we use, and the trade routes that have shaped our world. In motifs, traditions, and production processes, but also in power relations, memories, and identities.

For the Textile Biennial 2027, we invite (inter)national artists to reflect on the theme of Colonial patterns from the perspective of their own practice and perspective. You can submit a proposal via museumrijswijk.nl until October 1st, 2026, at 12:00 PM.

The Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns takes place from July 8 to November 21, 2027.

14131b9bb178eac979f90d05961bf4379e219c22.summary:
Source: Instagram #artopencall
OPEN CALL FOR ARTISTS

Strange Homes — “Where the familiar becomes uncertain.”

“ Home is often associated with comfort and belonging, but its meaning is neither stable nor universal. It can change across time and circumstance, shaped by where we live, what we remember, and how we understand ourselves in relation to others. Strange Homes explores these shifts, asking how something comes to feel like home, how that feeling can change, and what new meanings emerge when the familiar becomes uncertain.

No single experience defines home. The exhibition welcomes both personal and broader social perspectives, inviting artists to consider how ideas of home are formed, inherited, questioned, or reimagined, and how the familiar can take on different meanings over time. “

Rexhibit Online Gallery invites artists worldwide to submit work for Strange Homes, an international online group exhibition centered on the changing meanings of home.

AWARDS:
Gold Award — Online Solo Exhibition + Featured Interview
Silver Award — Online Solo Exhibition
Bronze Award — Featured Interview
Honorable Mention — Special recognition

Selected artists receive a dedicated exhibition presentation, digital catalog, promotional support, optional artwork inquiry feature, and consideration for future Rexhibit projects.

All mediums are welcome.

SUBMISSION FEE:
$18 for 1–3 works
$20 for 4–8 works

DEADLINE:
October 1, 2026

Is Formal Education Important?

What is formal education when it comes to art?
Who sets the educational programs?
Why?
Who is benefiting?
What is the benifit?
What gain is it for the fresh artists in a struggling market?
Why do they study past artists who did not study?
Why are some educated artists like those prof. try to award ME a prize THAT I PAY FOR, at a museum they rented, (see my previous reel about it, they have the last name Dr. Russo) only when I just started recently and am relevantly small compared to other? Oh yes, I know why... it is because they make me pay for it.... But what does that say about their art education? Or should I just blindly trust them because they have it?
....

Open Call | What Remains? International Juried Exhibition 

Asian Art Contemporary™ invites submissions for the virtual exhibition What Remains?, a showcase exploring what persists after moments, places, relationships, and ways of life have changed or disappeared. Artists Jennifer Ling Datchuk jenniferlingdatchuk, Kazuhito Kawai kazuhitokawai, and Yeonsu Ju yeonsuju, together with Ben Hsiao s1101_km, Co-Founder and Director of Artemin Gallery artemin.gallery, have been invited as jurors for this open call. Bringing perspectives across artistic and institutional practices, their selections will reflect the exhibition’s interest in diverse approaches to memory, transformation, and the traces that endure over time. What Remains seeks works that consider remnants not simply as evidence of what has been lost, but as active forms through which experiences can be revisited, reinterpreted, and given new meaning.

Who Can Apply
▪️Open to Asian artists worldwide, at all career stages.
▪️All traditional and digital media are welcome, including painting, sculpture, photography, video, mixed media, and more.
▪️Submitted work must be original, and artists are responsible for copyright compliance.

Selected Artist Benefits
▪️Virtual Exhibition: Work presented in a curated online exhibition.
▪️Artist Interview: Complimentary interview highlighting each artist’s practice and story.
▪️Social Media Promotion: Promotion through our official Instagram account.

c8325f6e888ed7b635a1397d475bf03fe61d7b5a.title: 90 Sekunden. So viel Zeit hat eine Jurymappe im Schnitt beim ersten Durchgang.
c8325f6e888ed7b635a1397d475bf03fe61d7b5a.summary:
Source: Instagram #artgrant
90 Sekunden. So viel Zeit hat eine Jurymappe im Schnitt beim ersten Durchgang.
Was in dieser Zeit passiert:
Das erste Bild entscheidet, ob überhaupt weitergeblättert wird - es trägt mehr Gewicht als jedes andere.
Konsistenz der Werkgruppe zählt mehr als ein einzelnes starkes Bild dazwischen.
Rechtschreibfehler im Anschreiben fallen in der ersten Minute auf und bleiben im Kopf.
Unklare Struktur kostet Zeit, die die Jury nicht hat - und Zeit, die sie nicht gibt.
Das heißt nicht: alles muss perfekt sein. Es heißt: die ersten Eindrücke verdienen die meiste Sorgfalt.

What if the traditional art exhibition was just the beginning of a work's impact?

We are thrilled to announce that applications for the Emerging Artists for Impact Award 2026 are officially open.

At the IAP Foundation, we are bringing talented emerging artists together, distributing $32,000 in awards, and showcasing their work on a global stage during Miami Art Week.

But our ambition goes much further. We are building a model where art generates both professional opportunity for the creator and measurable change for communities:

20 artists. 20 artworks. Our goal: 20 impact projects.
We are working to connect each selected artwork to tangible initiatives across five key areas: 💧 Clean Water 👥 Children & Youth 📖 Education Access 📈 Economic Empowerment 🌱 Environmental & Community Restoration

Turn art into lasting impact. The jury judges the art. Then the art goes to work.

How you can help: If you are an arts educator, curator, or industry professional, please share this opportunity with your network. Sometimes an opportunity only matters if the right person hears about it.

Eligible applicants include current BFA/MFA students and recent graduates (within two years) from accredited U.S. institutions.

🗓️ Applications close: September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET.

Apply now National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus Key dates Applications close Tuesday 13 October 2026 at 3pm AEDT Activity must start from 27 January 2027 and be completed by 31 December 2027 Amount Between $5,000 & $100,000 in matched funding. Contact If you need advice about eligibility and the program, contact Music Australia . If you need advice on how to register in our system, contact an Artists Services Officer . Apply now You must be registered in our Application Management System to apply for a grant. Registrations take up to two business days to process. NOTE: You will not be able to apply to the Tuesday 13 October 2026 closing date unless you register before 10am AEDT on Monday 12 October 2026. Registrations received after this time will not be processed until Wednesday 14 October. About the program The National Songwriting and Recording in Schools Stimulus (NSRSS) provides targeted matched funding to support high quality, inclusive songwriting and recording programs in schools, TAFEs, universities and other music academies across Australia. The program is for students/learners, educators and their partners. Program priorities Priority will be given to activities that: strengthen access to songwriting and recording opportunities for students, including those in regional, remote, outer suburban or under-served communities (the Accessibilty/Remoteness Index of Australia (ARIA) helps determine if your location is metropolitan, regional, remote or very remote – you can download the ARIA Code list from our website ). promote inclusive and equitable participation are First Nations-led or demonstrate strong First Nations partnership and cultural integrity build connections between learning and pathways or next step opportunities demonstrate strong local partnership and community benefit create sustainable or repeatable models rather than one-off activity increase teacher, mentor and provider capability strengthen contemporary music practice, including collaboration and creative development create teaching, mentoring or co-delivery opportunities for emerging or working composers, songwriters, producers and engineers, with priority given to those based locally to the delivery area. Please read the following guidelines for further information. If you need advice about applying contact Music Australia . Image: Birdland, Mount Lawley High School Expand all Collapse all Eligibility Who can apply government primary and secondary schools Catholic and independent primary and secondary schools school clusters or regional school consortia private music academies specialist music providers TAFEs Australian universities community conservatoria consortia including at least one educational institution Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) local councils music charities and foundations. The applying organisation must be located in Australia, majority Australian owned, and have been operating for a minimum of two years. The proposed activity must meet the Music Australia Council’s agreed definition of contemporary music, as follows: “Australian contemporary music is any genre or subgenre of music currently composed, written, produced by Australians and licensed, recorded, presented, and distributed through commercial and non-commercial activity. For the purposes of Music Australia’s investments, the focus is on musical works that are new, original and relevant to contemporary Australia.” The intention of this fund is to invest in programs that enable equity of access to songwriting and recording initiatives. d9f5b657bd4aca08a334b1f0ff238091d5dd9b6e.summary:
Source: Instagram #artprize
Steve Buccellato has chosen the winners of this year's art prize, and we'd like to start the announcements with the artists who didn't make the top prizes, but Steve felt deserved an acknowledgement.

Our next shout out goes to Frank Freire frankfreireffs , congrats Frank! You made Steve's job really difficult with your terrific work.

From Steve:

"Wow, this was a tough assignment! The volume of entries was intimidating enough, but comparing works from such varied genres, styles and mediums was quite a challenge. It almost doesn’t seem fair to compare some of the more divergent works with one another!

That being said, I approached the task by deciding on some universal criteria that could apply to all styles and genres, so I could judge each on their own merits. Those criteria included elements of craft, such as composition, anatomy, color theory, but also more intangible or subjective criteria like “overall feels,” individuality, and storytelling– which, to me, is one of the most important elements of a successful illustration."

INTERNATIONAL OPEN CALL 🌌

Slavic Spirit in Contemporary Art

Does your work echo ancient beliefs, symbols, and connections with nature? Do you seek in art that which is primal, mystical, and rooted in our shared identity?

We are launching an unique project that will connect artists from across the Slavic region (and Lithuania, which is culturally close to us). We are looking for painters, sculptors, and contemporary artists whose work explores Slavic roots, mythology, spirituality, and cosmogony.

 We are creating an international platform that will serve as a prelude to two major events in 2027:

🏛️ The International Exhibition of Painting and Sculpture "The Slavic Spirit in Contemporary Art" (March 20–21, 2027) at the prestigious REYMONTÓWKA  Creative Work Center in Chlewiska, Masovia, Poland.

 ⛰️ The three artists selected in the first stage at "Reymontówka" will be eligible to participate free of charge in the 10-day International Artistic Plein Air "In Luce-slavic artists  in Liguria" (September 21-30, 2027) in the picturesque mountain village of Villa Faraldi, Italy.

🌍 Who are we inviting?

We are looking for artists from Bulgaria, Bielarus, Bosnia&Herzegovina, Croatia, Lithuania, Macedonia Nord, Montenegro, Poland, Serbia, Slovakia, Słowenia and Ukraine

📩 How to join us?

Send us a short message to: krzysztofagorecki@gmail.com, including:

A few sentences about yourself and your inspiration for the Slavic spirit.

A link to your portfolio or 2-3 photos of your sig

Our next shout out goes to meghan_hetrick , congrats Meghan! Steve picked your piece "The Surgeon" as one that made him wonder what was going to happen next.

From Steve:

"Wow, this was a tough assignment! The volume of entries was intimidating enough, but comparing works from such varied genres, styles and mediums was quite a challenge. It almost doesn’t seem fair to compare some of the more divergent works with one another!

That being said, I approached the task by deciding on some universal criteria that could apply to all styles and genres, so I could judge each on their own merits. Those criteria included elements of craft, such as composition, anatomy, color theory, but also more intangible or subjective criteria like “overall feels,” individuality, and storytelling– which, to me, is one of the most important elements of a successful illustration."

John Ruskin Prize: Not for Present Delight – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu John Ruskin Prize: Not for Present Delight Deadline: Deadline: November 17 The John Ruskin Prize returns for its ninth year, inviting artists, designers and makers from anywhere in the world to submit work responding to the theme Not for Present Delight . Taking its title from the writings of John Ruskin, this year’s theme asks whether art must serve a purpose beyond itself, or whether it can exist simply for pleasure. It also considers what it means to create with an awareness of consequence in a time defined by environmental urgency and social inequality. The prize is open to amateur and professional artists, designers and makers working across any 2D or 3D medium, including drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, photography, textiles, animation, digital art, performance, installation and mixed media. Up to 80 selected works will be exhibited at Trinity Buoy Wharf in London. Four major prizes total £9,500: 1st Prize — £3,000 Alan Davidson Under 26 Prize — £1,000 Ruskin Mill Trust Prize — £3,000 Chelsea Arts Club Trust Prize — £2,500 International artists do not have to ship physical work if selected; they can choose to exhibit digitally instead. https://www.ruskinprize.co.uk/ Info not available info@parkerharris.co.uk

This edition explores ART + TECHNOLOGY the relationship between the handmade and the machine, the analogue and the digital, memory and invention, craft and automation, the organic and the artificial.

I want to see what technology means to you whether that’s through painting, photography, sculpture, textiles, poetry, illustration, digital work, writing, mixed media, or something entirely ditterent.

Source: Instagram #artopencall
// Issue 75 - Clay Every Which Way //

Clay is one of humanity's oldest creative companions. It records fingerprints, holds memory, cracks under pressure, hardens through fire, and can return to the earth. It exists somewhere between permanence and impermanence, control and chance, utility and expression... 

For this issue of HAUS-A-REST, we invited artists to explore Clay Every Which Way. We are interested in clay beyond the pot, beyond tradition, beyond expectation.

We selected work that embraces ceramics, sculpture, installation or functional objects.

The clay appears only as an idea, a metaphor for transformation, identity, labour, geology, archaeology, ritual, play, memory, or the body itself.

The work spans the use of unfired clay, clay slips, earth pigments, digital clay simulation, or explores landscapes where clay is found.

This issue also explores repetition, touch, repair, fragility, resilience, or the relationship between maker and material.

This year, the awards move to a single Open Category, inviting photographers to submit work across all genres from portraiture and landscape to documentary, wildlife, experimental, and contemporary practices. Rather than dividing photography into separate categories, the awards recognise that today’s image-making often moves fluidly across styles and disciplines. The judging committee will select five winning images from the pool of entries that best represent where Australian photography is at in 2026. Students currently enrolled in a recognised course may also opt into a Student Category at no additional cost when submitting a paid entry. The awards remain committed to photography grounded in original image capture. While digital editing is permitted, AI-generated imagery is not accepted, and any AI-assisted editing must be disclosed during the entry process. APA Exhibition & Event Program Finalists and shortlisted artists will be exhibited through print and projection as part of an exhibition program. Taking place in Naarm/Melbourne during July 2026. The APA Exhibition & Event Program will bring together artists and photographers from across Australia to share their work, make connections and celebrate photography. Introducing the 2026 Committee This year we’ve refined our approach, bringing together a focused committee to guide the award’s direction. With one category and multiple prizes, this group will work collaboratively to recognise the most compelling work submitted, drawing on the insight of leading Australian image makers, curators and educators who will consider this year’s entrants and champion standout photography. Open Call for Artists: FOCUS & FOCUS compact

Submissions are now open for Issue 4 of VERMEER Magazine.

For every issue, our FOCUS section introduces selected contemporary realist artists through one outstanding work. Artists can be selected for one of two formats: FOCUS, a two-page feature dedicated to one artist with an artwork and editorial texts about the work and artist, or FOCUS compact, where several selected artists are presented together across two pages with one artwork and a concise accompanying text each. Both formats are selected through the same open call.

To apply, send 3–5 high-resolution images of different works to editorial@vermeer-magazine.com. Please include captions for each work (title, year, size and technique), your full name and contact details, website, a text about the submitted artwork (max. 200 words) and a text about yourself as an artist (max. 200 words). One artwork will be selected for publication.

The submission fee is 25 CHF (approx. 24 GBP / 27 EUR / 32 USD; the daily exchange rate applies) and can be paid via PayPal to lichtschlag@freiheitsfunken.info. The fee covers the editorial review and participation in the selection process. Please note that submission does not guarantee publication and the fee is non-refundable.

*OPEN CALL* Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns

Colonial patterns are all around us; visible in the clothing we wear, the materials and fabrics we use, and the trade routes that have shaped our world. In motifs, traditions, and production processes, but also in power relations, memories, and identities.

For the Textile Biennial 2027, we invite (inter)national artists to reflect on the theme of Colonial patterns from the perspective of their own practice and perspective. You can submit a proposal via museumrijswijk.nl until October 1st, 2026, at 12:00 PM.

The Textile Biennial 2027 | Colonial patterns takes place from July 8 to November 21, 2027.

a58df4b084e55eaeee99a24bd79855863667bc32.summary: Impact Investment Readiness Program | Creative Australia Skip to main content Capability development Multi-art form Opening Soon Impact Investment Readiness Program Build a stronger, more sustainable organisation. Impact Investment Readiness Program Stage 1 Key Dates Online information session: to be announced Expression of Interest (EOI) opens: Monday 12 October 2026 EOI closes : Friday 30 October 2026, 3pm AEDT Notification of outcomes for EOI and invitation to Stage 2: by 13 November 2026 Stage 2 Key Dates Full Applications (invitation only): by Friday 20 November 2026 Notification of Stage 2 outcomes : December 2027 Program commences : 15 February 2027 Program ends : 15 May 2027 Contact If you have a question about eligibility, or need help with your application, please email . Social Enterprise Finance Australia (Sefa) Find out more about Sefa, our delivery partner, here . About the program The Impact Investment Readiness Program is being delivered in partnership between Creative Australia and Social Enterprise Finance Australia (Sefa). It supports creative and cultural organisations to strengthen their foundations, build long-term sustainability and explore impact investment as a potential source of capital. Arts organisations make a vital contribution to Australia’s cultural, social and economic life. Many, however, face challenges securing the capital needed to invest in growth and future sustainability. Impact investing offers an alternative pathway that seeks both measurable social, cultural or environmental impact and financial returns. Through the program, organisations will strengthen their business capability, better understand and articulate their impact, use evidence to support decision-making, and build confidence in planning for their future. Image: The Hum feat. artists of The Australian Ballet and artists of Australian Dance Theatre. Photo: Daniel Boud Program overview Expand all Collapse all Why does impact investing readiness matter? Investment readiness is more than accessing finance. Investment readiness means you can clearly articulate your impact in front of funders, have stronger business, governance and financial management in place and a clear plan to future proof your organisation. What you will learn and apply Through the program, participants will build practical knowledge, skills and tools to strengthen organisational sustainability, impact and readiness for future growth. You will learn how to: articulate, measure and communicate the impact of your work through a theory of change and impact measurement framework identify opportunities for income stream diversification and what needs to be in place to make this happen strengthen business planning for organisational sustainability and growth develop a growth/sustainability strategy and implementation plan aligned with your mission and impact identify and assess future funding options best suited to you, including impact investment. These skills can help organisations to: demonstrate impact to attract new partners, supporters, collaborators improve strategic planning and decision-making strengthen organisational sustainability and resilience prepare and pursue future growth opportunities. While the program supports organisations to build investment readiness, the skills, tools and frameworks developed will benefit participants regardless of whether impact investment is ultimately the right pathway for their organisation. What is involved The Impact Investment Readiness Program is delivered online over 14 weeks and combines practical learning, expert guidance and peer engagement to help organisations learn and apply new skills directly to their work. Participants will receive: self-paced online learning modules practical tools and templates online group sessions to exchange learnings with other peer organisations online individual coaching support to enhance application (Stream 1 participants only). The program will support up to 20 organisations

Patrick's ability to cross and often combine seemingly disparate art genres sees a distinct and elegant collision of beautifully fabricated imaginings with prose poetry, cabinetry, lighting and sound recordings. These often emotive pieces are rich in story-telling, sometimes autobiographical, sometimes not. Patrick is represented in public and private collections including the Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery, Hobart; the Museum of Old and New Art [MONA], Berriedale; the Power House Museum, Sydney and the National Gallery of Australia, Canberra. Bob Brown Bob Brown is an Australian former politician, medical doctor, artist, writer, and environmentalist. Bob's most recent book is Defiance. Bob is also an avid photographer and has held numerous solo exhibitions throughout Tasmania and on the mainland. After Bob left the Senate in 2012 he set up the Bob Brown Foundation to take peaceful direct action to stop environmental vandalism, to protect Tasmania’s Takayna rainforest, wildlife and Aboriginal heritage and to end native forest logging nationwide. From leading the seven-year campaign to save Tasmania's wild Franklin River from damming, through fifty-years of finding alternatives to humanity's rapid destruction of life on Earth, Bob Brown's credo has always been 'one person, one vote, one value, one planet'. Peter Johnson Peter Johnson’s ceramic works reflect memory and experience of the Australian landscape visible in the remnants of our industrial, suburban and maritime places, memories of daily living on the land and the expansiveness of the rural environment. For over 35 years Peter has maintained an active studio practice including the Jam Factory, Jamboree Clay Workshop and currently at Gaff Studio, Port Adelaide. For many years he lectured in Ceramics and Visual Arts at TAFE Adelaide College of Arts, O’Halloran Hill and Adelaide campuses. He has had artistic residencies in Barcelona, Spain with the Australia Council and Jingdezhen, China with the Helpmann Academy. Peter’s ceramic work has been shown locally, interstate and internationally. 74c5dcc6675b4cf732e40c003d6e991c4e7beab7.summary: Deadline: November 30. Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting – BNE ART - Brisbane Art Guide Skip to content Menu Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting Deadline: Deadline: November 30 The Elaine Bermingham National Watercolour Prize in Landscape Painting is a triennial award presented by Griffith University’s Queensland College of Art and Design, celebrating excellence and innovation in watercolour. The prize is open to Australian artists over the age of 18. The overall winner will receive a $20,000 non-acquisitive cash prize , generously donated by Elaine Bermingham. For the purposes of the prize, landscape is defined broadly as any form of land or environment. Peopled landscapes, seascapes, urbanised environments and rural habitats are all eligible. Works do not need to be representational, with innovative and abstracted approaches to watercolour welcomed. Finalists will be selected for an exhibition at QCAD Galleries at Griffith University’s Brisbane City Campus, South Bank. ANZANG bioregion means Australia, New Zealand, Antarctica and the New Guinea region. The region of New Guinea is limited to the west by the Wallace Line (the bio-geographical line extending between Bali and Lombok northward through the Makassar Strait between Borneo and Sulawesi). To the east the New Guinea region includes the Bismarck and Solomon Archipelagos and islands of the South West Pacific, with its eastern boundary formed by the International Date Line. Note that for the purposes of this competition, our definition of the Wallace Line does not include Huxley’s modification, and therefore the islands of the Philippines are not included in our definition of the ANZANG bioregion. Antarctica includes the Sub-Antarctic Islands, which for the purposes of this competition are those south of the Antarctic Convergence or Antarctic Polar Front. Entries in all sections are invited from photographers who use either digital or film cameras. Judges will consider the photographic technique plus the aesthetic, artistic and unique quality of all images when making their selections. Black and white and monochrome images (including infrared) may only be entered in the Monochrome or Junior categories. There are ten categories in the Competition. Up to four images may be entered in each category. The categories are: Animals in Nature – the subject(s) must be photographed in their natural environment. The animal(s) depicted may be either native or feral but must be depicted in nature with minimal evidence of human activity. Captive species are not allowed. Animal Behaviour

Source: Instagram #artopencall
Puddle gallery is launching an open call for its Fall 2026 show called I thought California would be different ! It is scheduled to open on November 7 in Koreatown 🏖️

Open call deadline is Sunday, October 11 at 11:59 pm

Application link in the bio 🏝️

I thought California Would Be Different takes its title from Raymond Pettibon’s No Title (I Thought California Would Be Different) and uses the phrase as a starting point rather than a conclusion. The exhibition considers the distance between an imagined California and the one we actually encounter: a place so heavily pictured in advance through ideas of sunlight, freedom, reinvention, beauty, glamour, success and failure that arriving here can feel like meeting something you already know. 

We invite work that responds to what happens when those expectations shift — through disappointment or disillusionment, but also through affection, surprise, belonging, or the discovery that California is stranger, richer, or better than anticipated. The prompt can be approached literally, personally, politically, humorously, or abstractly; we are interested in the many ways a real place exceeds, contradicts, fulfills, or transforms the version of it we carried with us.

Was oft nicht im Angebot steckt:
Anreisekosten - viele Programme decken nur Aufenthalt und Arbeitsraum, nicht den Flug oder Zug dorthin.
Verpflegung vor Ort ist oft teurer als zuhause kalkuliert, besonders in touristischen Regionen.
Während des Aufenthalts fällt reguläres Einkommen aus zuhause weg - das rechnet kaum jemand vorher durch.
Materialkosten vor Ort sind selten im Stipendium enthalten, auch wenn 'Arbeitsraum gestellt' klingt wie alles inklusive.
Vor Zusage genau nachfragen, was konkret gedeckt ist - nicht nach der Ankunft überrascht werden.

横浜 元町のDiffractionにて
ジャンル不問の小作品展を開催します。

贈り物シーズンに、手仕事の小作品を展示してみませんか？

ショップ・カフェを併設した
穏やかな時間をお過ごしいただける空間です。

応募締切：11.10 または審査通過者で枠が埋まり次第

以下リンクよりご応募いただけます🔗
https://diffraction.jp/entry/

【Small Works Show】

・会期：12.10 – 12.27 
・会場：Diffraction
　〒 231-0868 横浜市中区石川町1-43-2
・応募締切：11.10 または審査通過者で枠が埋まり次第
────────────────────────
【募集内容】
・1人5点まで応募可能（デジタル作品不可）
・壁面展示作品：35×35cm 以内推奨（ピクチャーレールにて展示）
・立体作品（置き型）：底面 30×30 cm以内
・販売価格は税込30,000円以内を推奨
✴︎ 版画・陶芸など複数制作可能で補充用在庫がある作品は即売可能
✴︎ 同作品の補充用在庫追加の出展料：無料
（搬入時に補充用在庫も2点までお預けいただけます）

────────────────────────
【参加費】審査無料、選考通過者のみ
・1作品 税込¥ 7,000、5点まで
────────────────────────
【スケジュール】
・搬入：11.16 – 12.05（営業時間内・水曜定休）
・搬出：12.27 18:30–20:00（または後日回収相談可） 

販売手数料30%
非売品のご出展も可能(お申込時にお知らせください)

✴︎ 小作品展へのお申込みの流れ ✴︎
①https://diffraction.jp/entry/より、「会期」でグループ展の開催予定日：2026/12/10〜12/27を選択し、作家情報・作品情報（作品・サイズ）を入力後、展示希望作品の画像を添付の上、ご応募ください。

②審査後、通過された方には担当者よりメールにて確認事項・お支払い情報・同意書等の詳細についてご案内いたします。

③参加費のお振込後、指定期間内に搬入にお越しください。
（郵送での搬入の場合は事前にお知らせください。）

素敵な作品のご応募をお待ちしております。

Diffraction

✴︎注意事項
・過去2回以上当ギャラリーの公募展に応募された方は、審査結果を問わず本展へのご応募はご遠慮ください。（所属先の別団体などであれば応募可）
・審査を通過した作品の出展キャンセルは原則お断りしています。
